THE RA.MAYANA OF VAL.MIKI 
King Dasaratba, reigning over the earth, had none superior 
or equal to himseJ£ Honoured by his feudal lords, surrounded 
by friends. King Dasaratha, like Indra, reigned in majesty. 
Benevolent, powerful, accomplished and gracious, King 
Dasaratba protected Ayodhya and shone in splendour like the

KING DASARATBA, that glorious and righteous king, though 
performing great austerities, was without an heir to the thtone. 
Then the wise and great-souled monarch said to himself: " I

a son." 
Having thus decided, the supremely sagacious sovereign 
convened a meeting of his counsellors and addressing his chief 
minister, Sumantra, commanded him as follows : " Send 
speedily for the spiritual preceptors and priests." Quick to act, 
Sumantra at once summoned those highly learned preceptors 
and brought thither Suyagna, Vamadeva, Javali, Kasyapa 
and Vasishtha together with other eminent priests and 
brahmins. 
Having offered salutations to these holy men, King Dasaratha, 
speaking in gracious accents, uttered words full of truth and 
purpose : He said, "0 Sages, 1 have practised virtue and yet

The learned bnhmins, led by Shri Vasishtha, praised the 
king's intention and said : " Thou hast decided on the ptoper

chosen on the north bank of the rivet Sarayu. 0 King, 
this holy resolve formed by thee, for the sake of an heir, will 
assuredly bring the fulfilment of thy desire ". 
Hearing the words of the brabmins, the monarch rejoiced and 
commanded his ministets to bring the sactificial appointments

they were also directed to erect a sactificial pavilion on the bank

The king said : " Let it be remembered that during the

By cartying through the ritual without

The counsellors replied, saying, " 0 King, be it so ". 
Blessing the monarch, the learned brahmins retired, and the

ity for its final success." 
Then the illustrious sovereign left the court and enteted his

brief.summary_1line: King Dasaratha, troubled by his lack of an heir, resolves to perform the Ashvamedha sacrifice and orders preparations with priests and ministers.

image_candidates.scene_text: King Dasaratha stands before assembled sages and ministers in his court, declaring his resolve to perform the Ashvamedha sacrifice for a son.
Priests and warriors release the sacred horse to roam freely as the Ashvamedha ritual begins.
The queens of Ayodhya smile with brightened lotus-like faces as King Dasaratha tells them he will perform a sacrifice to obtain a son.
